evidence: One row per respondent to the 1969 Psychology Today survey ('Cross-section data'); rating is the respondent's 'self rating of marriage' from 1 to 5, a covariate rather than an id, and the page fits lm, probit, tobit, Poisson, negative binomial and zero-inflated models of affairs (Greene 2003, Tab. 22.3-22.6); no unit repeats.

year ('factor indicating year') is the March CPS survey wave, seven waves 1992-2004 of 2482 to 3744 workers each, no worker repeating, but the page's interaction.plot(year, gender, earnings) and Stock and Watson (2007, Table 3.1) compare men's and women's mean earnings separately per year ('trends (from 1992 to 2004) in hourly earnings'), so the table keeps its filing (GSSvocab).

One row per NMES respondent aged 66 and over ('Cross-section data'); hospital ('Number of hospital stays') and school ('Number of years of education') are counts, medicaid ('Is the individual covered by Medicaid?') a yes/no factor and region four levels, a design factor, and the page fits Poisson, negative binomial, hurdle and zero-inflated models of visits; no unit repeats.

One row per married woman of Mroz (1987) ('Cross-section data originating from the 1976 Panel Study of Income Dynamics'); city ('Does the individual live in a large city?') is a yes/no attribute, which the page's lm(wage ~ experience + I(experience^2) + education + city) fits fixed beside its probit, tobit and selection models (Greene 2003; Winkelmann and Boes 2009); no woman repeats.

One row per strike begun in June of a year 1968-1976 ('Greene (2003) only provides the June data for each year'); uoutput ('unanticipated output') takes one value per year, which no column holds, a stand-in and no id, and the page fits survreg(Surv(duration) ~ uoutput, dist = 'weibull') (Greene 2003, Example 22.10).

One row per household (idcase, 'a cross-section' of 'households') with one choice of heating system, depvar; the five alternatives' costs ic.*, oc.* and pb.* are attributes of that one choice rather than repeated measures, and region has four levels, a design factor; a single-level choice model, as its copy pymc_examples heating_data_r.csv was read.

One row per contract strike, 1968-1976 (Kennan 1985; 'a cross-section'); gdp, the 'deviation of monthly log industrial production' in the strike's month, takes one value per month, which no column holds, a stand-in and no id, and Cameron and Trivedi (2005, pp. 574-5 and 582) fit duration models of dur.

The yearly terrorism incidents 1970-2020 are columns, one row per country ('the numbers of incidents and numbers of deaths by year and by location of the event for 204 countries (rows)'), 1993 missing and the countries row names; the long form is country x year, which no registry object or other table holds, Ecdat's terrorism giving only the world and US totals per year.

The yearly terrorism deaths 1970-2020 are columns, one row per country ('the numbers of incidents and numbers of deaths by year and by location of the event for 204 countries (rows)'), 1993 missing and the countries row names; the long form is country x year, which no registry object or other table holds, Ecdat's terrorism giving only the world and US totals per year.

One row per worker of two CPS cross sections ('compiled these data from the 1978 and 1985 Current Population Surveys'), no worker repeating; year ('78 or 85') has two levels, a design factor, which Example 13.2 fits fixed by the y85 interactions the table holds (y85, y85fem, y85educ, y85union).

One row per mother (Angrist and Evans 1998, 'black or Hispanic women'); weeks ('weeks worked mom') counts weeks rather than indexing a unit, and the text (pages 530-531) uses samesex as an instrument for kids; no unit repeats.

One row per released North Carolina prisoner (Chung, Schmidt and Witte 1991); person ('=1 if crime against person') is a crime-type indicator rather than an id, and the text's duration models (pages 611-612, 625) fit durat censored by cens; no prisoner repeats.

One row per joblessness spell of a displaced worker (CPS Displaced Workers Supplements 1986-1992); year85, year87 and year89 ('= 1 if year of job loss is 1985') code a few job-loss years and midatl to pacific the nine census divisions, design factors, and stateur ('state unemployment rate') takes one value per state and year, which no column holds, a stand-in and no id; MMA 17.11 fits duration models of spell.

One row per man of the NLS Young Men (id 'identification code', one row each; Card 1995); region ('census region in 1966') holds the nine census divisions, a design factor, and the 1966 columns (grade66, smsa66, age66) are baselines of the 1976 wage, which MMA 4.9.6 fits by IV regression of wage76 on grade76; no unit repeats.

tpos and tneg (vaccinated) and cpos and cneg (control) are each trial's TB positive and negative cases in its two arms as columns ('number of TB positive cases in the treated (vaccinated) group'), one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 BCG's arms, and the page's escalc RR with rma(yi, vi, mods = ~ ablat + year) pools them, year the publication year; no registry object or other table holds the long form, HSAUR3 BCG being the same 13 trials wide.

One row per movie (title); year ('The release year of the movie') dates each movie, 44 years of 1 to 129 movies, a time covariate and no sampled unit, as beyondmlr kingCountyHouses' sale date; Bayes Rules! chapter 4 (bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-4) fits a Beta-Binomial of the pass rate on one year's movies per analyst (1991, 2000, 2013), and no model groups by year.

One row per U.S. state ('50 observations, one per state'); region ('region in which the state falls') has four levels, a design factor, and Bayes Rules! chapter 12 (bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-12) fits Normal and Poisson regressions of laws ~ percent_urban + historical without region or grouping; no unit repeats.

Daily weather at one station ('A sub-sample of daily weather information on Perth'), one row per day; year, month and day_of_year are calendar indices of sampled days, not units (bayesrules weather_australia, bikes), and Bayes Rules! chapter 13 (bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-13) fits stan_glm(raintomorrow ~ humidity9am + humidity3pm + raintoday, family = binomial) without grouping.

time and timef are each race's record times for males and females ('record time in hours for males', 'record time in hours for females') as columns, one row per race, as DAAG ironslag's two methods; the page fits lm(log(time) ~ log(dist) + log(climb)) on the male times alone, and no registry object or other table holds the race x sex long form, lognihills being the logged copy.

mouse_id indexes the 73 mice whose 181 serum samples repeat within them ('multiple serums per mouse were taken'), BeyondArena's group_on, but its target HasCancer is one label per mouse (group_labels 'per_group'), so the one-label rule keeps its filing.

code_module and code_presentation index the module presentations whose registrations repeat within them (7 modules in 4 presentations of 4684 to 11260 rows each), and id_student repeats for students registered in several, the factors studentInfo.csv's registry row fits as (1 | code_module:code_presentation) + (1 | id_student), but the table is the registration lookup ('information about the time when the student registered for the module presentation', Kuzilek et al. 2017) keyed as studentInfo.csv's rows, with no outcome, so it stays excluded by the lookup rule.
